title: MiCA stablecoin treasury: a practical guide for EU corporate treasurers
linkedinPost:
128% growth in euro stablecoin market cap in 12 months. As of 1 July 2026, the EU's MiCA transitional period is closed — and the risk picture for corporate treasurers changed overnight.

This is not a crypto story. It is a treasury governance story.

MiCA creates 2 instruments that matter: E-Money Tokens (EMTs, the practical standard for B2B settlements) and Asset-Referenced Tokens (ARTs, more complex, harder to use in standard treasury contexts). USDT has no MiCA authorisation. Any EU corporate using it for settlements now has a compliance exposure, not just a market risk.

What I would actually do:

• Audit every stablecoin instrument in use — payment teams often settle with stablecoins without treasury awareness
• Run the EMT checklist: MiCA authorisation number, Art. 36 reserve custody, redemption terms
• Check your custody provider holds both MiCA AND PSD2 coverage — the gap between the two is now your risk
• Build a stablecoin instrument register before your next regulatory examination
• If automating settlement, design to a typed abstraction layer — I use n8n + Supabase + Circle EURC for the EU rail

The Revenue Per Employee frame applies directly: automated MiCA-compliant settlement pipelines cut cross-border processing from 3–5 days to same-day. That is not a fintech innovation story. That is a treasury efficiency story.

Full piece + the MiCA Readiness Ladder I built around this — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What stablecoins are MiCA-compliant for EU corporate treasury in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of June 2026, approximately 8 euro-denominated EMTs hold MiCA authorisation. Circle's EURC and EU-issued USDC are the most widely used for corporate operations. USDT does not hold MiCA authorisation and cannot be used in regulated EU corporate settlements.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an EMT and an ART under MiCA for corporate treasury purposes?

acceptedAnswer.text: An EMT references a single fiat currency and must be issued by a bank or e-money institution — this is the standard instrument for B2B payments and cash management. An ART references a basket of assets and faces additional reserve and governance requirements, making it more complex for standard corporate treasury use.

mainEntity.name: Can a corporate treasurer hold MiCA-regulated stablecoins without a crypto licence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Holding and using MiCA-compliant stablecoins for payments does not require the treasury to hold a crypto licence — the licensing obligation sits with the issuer and custody/transfer service provider. The treasury's obligation is counterparty due diligence, instrument governance, and policy documentation.

mainEntity.name: What are the MiCA non-compliance penalties for corporate stablecoin use?

acceptedAnswer.text: For financial institutions, using non-authorised stablecoins can trigger concurrent supervisory findings under MiCA, DORA, and PSD2. For non-financial corporates, the primary risk is service interruption if your custody provider loses MiCA authorisation. Non-compliance fines for service providers reach 12.5% of annual turnover.
